title: Algebraization of equations coming from a pair henselization
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $S$ be a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $H$ be the henselization of $(S,IS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Write $\widehat S=\varprojlim_nS/I^nS$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], Let $\theta:\widehat S\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat H_{IH}$ be the canonical isomorphism of completions [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion], and put $\gamma=\theta^{-1}\circ(H\to\widehat H_{IH})$. For every ideal $Q\subseteq H$, let $Q\widehat S$ mean the ideal of $\widehat S$ generated by $\gamma(Q)$. Then there exist a finite type $A$-algebra $C$ and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat C_{IC}\cong\widehat S/Q\widehat S$.

source.place: Tag 0GAS (lemma-algebraize-easy), in the quotient-of-completion formulation used in the last displayed equality of the proof of proposition-approximate.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion] to $(S,IS)$: $H$ is Noetherian and its completion comparison is the canonical $S$-algebra isomorphism $\theta$ in the statement. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose finitely many generators $q_1,\ldots,q_m$ of $Q$; allow $m=0$ when $Q=0$.

Use the filtered colimit presentation of $H$ in [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], passing to a small skeleton using its essential smallness. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], each $q_j$ comes from an object of this diagram. Filteredness gives a common successor for these finitely many objects (iterate the common-successor property; for the empty family choose the identity object). Thus there are an $S$-algebra $D$, an etale morphism $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}S$, an isomorphism $S/IS\to D/ID$, its colimit map $f:D\to H$, and $d_j\in D$ with $f(d_j)=q_j$. Put $J=(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\subset D$ and $C=D/J$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], $D$ is generated over $S$ by finitely many elements $t_k$. If $s_i$ generate $S$ over $A$, then their images together with the $t_k$ generate $D$ over $A$: substitute the polynomials in the $s_i$ for the coefficients of a polynomial in the $t_k$. Their images generate $C=D/J$ because every class has a representative in $D$. Hence $D$ and $C$ are finite type $A$-algebras in the explicit sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], $S\to D$ is flat. Its reduction modulo $IS$ is an isomorphism by the choice of $D$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers], applied to the ideal $IS$ of $S$, gives compatible canonical isomorphisms $a_n:S/I^nS\to D/I^nD$ for all $n\ge1$. Applying these maps and their inverses coordinatewise to compatible sequences gives inverse $S$-algebra isomorphisms $a:\widehat S\to\widehat D_{ID}$ and $\beta=a^{-1}$. The inverses preserve compatibility since $a_n$ commute with all quotient transitions. Write $c_D:D\to\widehat D$ and $c_H:H\to\widehat H$. The map $f$ induces $\widehat f:\widehat D\to\widehat H$ coordinatewise; $\widehat f a=\theta$, since both maps on every quotient are induced by $S\to H$. Thus $\widehat f=\theta\beta$, and $\beta c_D=\theta^{-1}c_Hf=\gamma f$. Here the normalization of $\theta$ is exactly that in [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] over $D$, with ideal $ID$, to $0\to J\to D\to C\to0$. These are finite $D$-modules: $J$ is generated by the $d_j$, and $D,C$ are cyclic. The resulting map $\pi:\widehat D\to\widehat C_{IC}$ is a surjective ring map, because it is the coordinatewise quotient map. Its kernel is the image of $\widehat J\to\widehat D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], every element of $\widehat J$ is a finite sum of terms $b\,\iota_J(j)$ with $b\in\widehat D$, $j\in J$, and its image is $b c_D(j)$. Consequently $\ker\pi=J\widehat D=(c_D(d_1),\ldots,c_D(d_m))$: expand each $j$ in the generators $d_j$; conversely every $b c_D(j)$ is the image of $b\,\iota_J(j)$. Thus $\widehat D/J\widehat D\cong\widehat C_{IC}$, by sending a class to $\pi$ of any representative; the map is well-defined and bijective by the computed kernel and surjectivity. Under $\beta$, the ideal $J\widehat D$ becomes $(\gamma(q_1),\ldots,\gamma(q_m))=Q\widehat S$, since $q_j$ generate $Q$ and $\gamma$ is a ring map. Transporting the quotient isomorphism by $\beta$ and taking its inverse gives the required $A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat C_{IC}\cong\widehat S/Q\widehat S$.

The item states the quotient-of-completion form, which is exactly the form the parent's step 4 uses. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. This is a first split: the item had no proof before. There are no new nodes. Step checks: (1) 00FN makes S Noetherian. 0AGV applied with the ideal IS makes H Noetherian, and its comparison theta is the one induced by S->H; here I^h = IH. The definition of a Noetherian ring gives finitely many generators q_j of Q. (2) The pair-henselization category with (S, IS) is essentially small and directed, so it is filtered. The elementwise lemma (2) gives a representative of each q_j at some stage, and a common successor moves them all to one stage D, which is etale over S with S/IS ≅ D/ID. Injectivity of D->H is never used, and id_S covers m=0. (3) The finite-presentation lemma, clause (1), plus the finite-type definition make D and C = D/J of finite type over A, and D is Noetherian. (4) S->D is flat because it is etale. The flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers lemma applies with ideal IS, using (IS)^n D = I^n D, so a: S^ ≅ D^. Then f^ a = theta coordinatewise, which gives beta c_D = gamma f. (5) Completion is exact on finite modules over D with ideal ID applied to 0->J->D->C->0. The finite-module tensor comparison (2) for J, with the linearity of u^, gives ker = J D^ = (c_D(d_j)). Beta carries this ideal to gamma(Q) S^. Edge cases checked: Q=0, Q=H (d need not be a unit, yet the completion of C is 0), I=A and I=0 are all consistent. A search of dag/nodes for 0GAS or algebraize-easy finds only the item and its parent, so no duplicate. I accept the tool_uses entry for henselization-noetherian-completion. Note for the maintainer: flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers (sk-thm-p1, status split) is also used outside its unit as a generic tool and may also need recording in tool_uses. No SGA. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem henselian_equations_algebraization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] (hS : (algebraMap A S).FiniteType) (c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of S) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map D.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((I.map (algebraMap A S)).map D.hom.hom) D.hom.hom Ideal.le_comap_map)))) (hc : IsColimit c) (θ : AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A S)) S ≃+* AdicCompletion ((I.map (algebraMap A S)).map c.pt.hom.hom) c.pt.right) (hθ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A S)) S) (s : S), AdicCompletion.evalₐ (I.map (algebraMap A S)) n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((I.map (algebraMap A S)) ^ n) s → AdicCompletion.evalₐ ((I.map (algebraMap A S)).map c.pt.hom.hom) n (θ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (((I.map (algebraMap A S)).map c.pt.hom.hom) ^ n) (c.pt.hom.hom s)) (Q : Ideal c.pt.right) : ∃ (C : CommRingCat.{max u v}) (_ : Algebra A C), (algebraMap A C).FiniteType ∧ Nonempty (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C ≃ₐ[A] (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A S)) S) ⧸ Q.map (θ.symm.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap c.pt.right (AdicCompletion ((I.map (algebraMap A S)).map c.pt.hom.hom) c.pt.right))))
